summary_en: Model a deal, run scenarios, produce an investment memo.
summary_fr: Modéliser une opération, tester des scénarios, produire un mémo d'investissement.

tools.name: ARGUS Enterprise
tools.positioning: The cash-flow model the industry agreed to standardise on — a valuation is credible partly because it is an ARGUS file.
tools.description: ARGUS Enterprise models commercial property cash flows lease by lease: rent steps, recoveries, renewal probabilities, capital expenditure and debt, producing valuations, hold-sell analysis and portfolio consolidation. Its file format is a de facto industry exchange standard.
tools.real_estate_use: When an asset trades, the seller's broker sends an ARGUS file and the buyer re-underwrites in the same tool. That shared format is most of the value — assumptions are visible and comparable rather than buried in someone's private spreadsheet. Appraisers, lenders and fund managers use it for the same reason.
features: Lease-by-lease commercial cash flow modelling
Recovery structures, rent steps and market leasing assumptions
Valuation by discounted cash flow and direct capitalisation
Debt, equity waterfall and hold-sell analysis
Portfolio consolidation and scenario comparison
Industry-standard file exchange with counterparties

use_cases.job: Underwrite an acquisition from the seller's own cash flow model
Produce a valuation in the format lenders and auditors expect

tools.name: Cherre
tools.positioning: Not another data source — the layer that reconciles the twenty you already pay for onto one property identity.
tools.description: Cherre is a real estate data management platform. It ingests a firm's internal systems and its licensed third-party feeds, resolves them to a common property and entity identity, and exposes the result to BI tools and models. The product is the resolution and the connectors, not the underlying data.
tools.real_estate_use: A large owner-operator typically has the rent roll in Yardi, valuations in ARGUS, market data from a vendor and a dozen spreadsheets — with no shared key between them. Cherre matches them to one property record so that portfolio reporting stops being a quarterly manual reconciliation, and so that a model can be trained on something coherent.
features: Entity and address resolution to a single property identity
Prebuilt connectors to major real estate systems and data vendors
Managed warehouse with governed access
Data quality monitoring and lineage
Delivery to BI tools, notebooks and applications
Marketplace of third-party datasets

use_cases.job: Consolidate portfolio reporting across accounting, valuation and market systems
Give analysts one governed dataset instead of eight incompatible exports

tools.name: CoStar
tools.positioning: The commercial property database the industry underwrites against, built on a research organisation rather than on scraping.
tools.description: CoStar maintains a researched inventory of US commercial buildings — physical characteristics, ownership, tenancy, lease comparables, sale comparables, availabilities and submarket analytics — collected and verified by a large in-house research team and sold as a subscription with strict per-seat licensing.
tools.real_estate_use: It is the reference for the questions that precede a deal: what is the true rentable area, who owns the entity behind the LLC, what did the last three comparable leases sign at, what is the submarket vacancy trend. Brokers pull comparables for a pitch, investors size a market before underwriting, lenders sanity-check a borrower's rent roll.
features: Researched property records with ownership and tenancy detail
Lease and sale comparables with confirmed terms
Availability and vacancy tracking by submarket
Market analytics, forecasts and rent trends
Tenant tracking and expiring-lease intelligence
Directory of owners, brokers and tenants

use_cases.job: Size a submarket and pull comparable leases before underwriting an acquisition
Build a pitch on confirmed comparables rather than on asking rents

tools.name: Dealpath
tools.positioning: The deal pipeline for an investment team — what we looked at, what we passed on, and why.
tools.description: Dealpath is a deal management platform for real estate investment firms: pipeline tracking, underwriting data capture, task and approval workflows, document management and reporting across acquisitions, development and debt.
tools.real_estate_use: An acquisitions team screens far more deals than it buys, and the institutional memory of the ones it passed on is usually lost. Dealpath keeps every screened deal with its underwriting assumptions and its rejection reason, so a market can be re-approached with history intact and an investment committee can see the funnel rather than the survivors.
features: Deal pipeline with stage, status and ownership tracking
Structured underwriting data capture and comparison
Task, approval and investment committee workflows
Document repository per deal
Pipeline and market reporting for investment committees
Integrations with modelling and data providers

use_cases.job: Keep a defensible record of every deal screened and the reason it was passed
Give an investment committee a live view of the pipeline instead of a deck

capabilities: Document data extraction into deal records

tools.name: Horiz.io
tools.positioning: Rental investment analysis for the French private investor — yield, tax regime and cash flow before the offer is made.
tools.description: Horiz.io provides French rental investors with property analysis and simulation: gross and net yield calculation, comparison of tax regimes for furnished and unfurnished letting, financing and cash flow projection, plus portfolio tracking after acquisition.
tools.description_fr: Horiz.io propose aux investisseurs locatifs français l'analyse et la simulation de biens : calcul de rendement brut et net, comparaison des régimes fiscaux en location nue et meublée, projection de financement et de trésorerie, ainsi que le suivi du patrimoine après acquisition.
tools.real_estate_use: In France the tax regime often decides whether an investment works — the same apartment can be cash-flow negative unfurnished and positive under a furnished regime with amortisation. Comparing those scenarios by hand is where private investors get it wrong. Horiz models them side by side before the offer, and then tracks the actual result afterwards.
features: Gross, net and net-of-tax yield calculation
Comparison of French rental tax regimes side by side
Financing and cash flow projection over the hold period
Renovation and works scenario modelling
Portfolio tracking after acquisition
Report generation for a financing application

use_cases.job: Compare furnished and unfurnished tax regimes on the same property before offering
Project cash flow over the hold period including financing and works

tools.name: Juniper Square
tools.positioning: Investor relations for private real estate funds — the capital account, the distribution and the portal in one place.
tools.description: Juniper Square provides fund administration and investor management for private real estate: subscriptions and onboarding, capital calls and distributions, waterfall calculations, investor reporting and an LP portal, with an administration service option.
tools.real_estate_use: A sponsor raising from private investors has to track ownership across entities, calculate a promote correctly, and produce K-1 packages and quarterly reports that LPs trust. Getting that wrong is a relationship problem, not a bookkeeping one. Juniper Square replaces the spreadsheet-and-mail-merge approach with an auditable system and a portal LPs log into.
features: Investor onboarding with electronic subscription documents
Capital calls, distributions and capital account tracking
Waterfall and promote calculation
LP portal with documents, statements and tax packages
Fund and deal-level performance reporting
Optional outsourced fund administration

use_cases.job: Run capital calls and distributions across many entities without spreadsheet risk
Give private investors a portal with their statements and tax documents

tools.name: LEON
tools.positioning: Feasibility and financial-modeling tool that runs a social-housing developer's operations through underwriting and investment-committee approval.
tools.description: LEON is a French SaaS tool from Scepia used by social-housing developers to model and steer PLUS, PLAI and social/free accession housing operations. It runs financial-ratio simulations to check an operation's profitability, keeps national parameters and regulatory constraints up to date, and runs the investment-committee (comité d'engagement) process end to end — scheduling, document distribution, remote sessions, e-signed minutes and voting.
tools.real_estate_use: A social-housing developer's operations team enters a new PLUS or PLAI project and gets a first financial-ratio result within minutes, checking profitability before committing further work. Ahead of an investment committee, the same team schedules the session and distributes the operation's dossier and simulations through a web portal, and for groups running committees remotely, holds the session online with e-signed minutes and recorded votes.
features: Financial-ratio feasibility simulation
Built-in national/regulatory parameters for social housing
Investment-committee scheduling and document distribution
Remote committee sessions with e-signed minutes
Electronic voting

use_cases.job: Run a financial-ratio feasibility simulation for a new PLUS/PLAI operation before committing further work
Schedule and hold a remote investment committee with e-signed minutes and recorded votes

tools.name: Leonardo247
tools.positioning: Portfolio-wide operations and risk platform for property owners, covering due diligence, maintenance and student housing turns.
tools.description: Leonardo247 is a suite of modules for multifamily and student housing operators: Acquire247 runs unit-by-unit due diligence inspections before acquisition, Perform247 manages day-to-day maintenance workflows, inspections and code compliance, Protect247 runs preventative-maintenance risk workflows, Connect247 covers remote maintenance dispatch, and Student247 manages student-housing turn logistics such as key returns and vendor scheduling.
tools.real_estate_use: An operations manager overseeing a multifamily portfolio needs a single system to run acquisition due diligence, then keep every property compliant on preventative maintenance and inspections once it's owned — a missed fire-code inspection or a botched student-housing turn creates both risk and cost. Leonardo247 gives the team one platform across the acquisition-to-operations lifecycle instead of separate spreadsheets per phase.
features: Acquire247 acquisition due-diligence inspections
Perform247 maintenance and work-order workflows
Protect247 preventative-maintenance risk management
Connect247 remote maintenance dispatch
Student247 student-housing turn management
Portfolio-wide reporting and dashboards

use_cases.job: Run unit-by-unit due diligence inspections ahead of a multifamily acquisition
Track preventative maintenance and code-compliance inspections across a portfolio

tools.name: Lycaon Data
tools.positioning: Custom econometric reports and a SaaS dashboard that price a property's value drivers and market trajectory for real estate investors.
tools.description: Lycaon Data produces econometric analysis of real estate markets: custom reports built on deduplicated listing and transaction databases, modelling how individual property attributes affect value, and quantifying supply-demand gaps by quarter. It also runs a SaaS dashboard version of the same modelling.
tools.real_estate_use: An investment fund or developer evaluating a site asks Lycaon Data for a report on how specific attributes (surface, floor, exposure, local supply-demand balance) move price in that submarket, rather than relying on a generalist comparables tool. A bank or agency network uses the recurring dashboard to track the same supply-demand gap over time instead of commissioning a report each quarter.
features: Custom econometric valuation reports
Deduplicated listing and transaction databases
Property attribute impact modelling
Quarterly supply-demand gap analysis
SaaS dashboard version of the models

use_cases.job: Get a data-backed read on which property attributes drive value in a specific submarket before underwriting a deal
Quantify the local supply-demand gap for a planned development

tools.name: Northspyre
tools.positioning: Development cost control for the owner's side of the table, not the contractor's.
tools.description: Northspyre is a project cost management platform for real estate developers: budget tracking, invoice and contract processing with automated data extraction, cash flow forecasting, and anticipated cost reporting across a development pipeline.
tools.real_estate_use: A developer's exposure is the gap between the budget presented to investors and the anticipated final cost. That gap usually surfaces late because invoices and change orders are processed manually. Northspyre extracts the data as documents arrive, so the anticipated cost report updates continuously and a lender draw package is assembled from live data rather than rebuilt each month.
features: Automated data extraction from invoices and contracts
Budget versus anticipated cost tracking per project
Cash flow forecasting across a development pipeline
Lender draw package preparation
Vendor contract and change order tracking
Portfolio-level development reporting

use_cases.job: Keep anticipated final cost current instead of discovering the overrun late
Assemble a lender draw package from live project data

tools.name: Placer.ai
tools.positioning: Foot traffic as a leasing argument — how many people actually walk into this centre, and where else do they go.
tools.description: Placer.ai turns anonymised mobile location data into visit metrics for physical venues: visit counts, dwell time, trade-area maps, visitor demographics and cross-shopping between brands. Coverage is strongest in the US, with an expanding international footprint.
tools.real_estate_use: In retail leasing it replaces the argument from intuition. A landlord shows a prospective tenant that the centre draws a measured number of visits from a trade area matching the brand's customer profile. Investors use the same data to underwrite retail assets and to spot decline before it appears in the rent roll.
features: Visit counts and trends per venue and per chain
Trade-area maps and visitor origin analysis
Visitor demographics and psychographic segments
Cross-visitation between brands and centres
Site selection scoring for new locations
Void analysis and competitive benchmarking

use_cases.job: Underwrite a retail asset on measured footfall rather than on reported sales
Prove trade-area quality to a retail tenant during lease negotiation

capabilities: Visit estimation models from mobile location panels

tools.name: Salvia Développement
tools.positioning: Software for French property development operations — the bilan promoteur, the VEFA sales ledger and the cost control in one system.
tools.description: Salvia Software publishes solutions for French property developers and social housing operators covering development operation management: feasibility and operation budget, cost and commitment tracking, VEFA reservation and sale follow-up, calls for funds by construction stage, and operation profitability reporting.
tools.real_estate_use: A French development operation has a financial structure no generic tool models: the bilan promoteur, VEFA sales where the buyer pays by construction milestone, and a margin that moves with every signed contract and every works order. Salvia is bought to hold that structure — the operation budget and the sales ledger reconciled against one another.
features: Operation feasibility and bilan promoteur modelling
Cost, commitment and works contract tracking
VEFA reservation and sale follow-up
Calls for funds by construction milestone
Operation and portfolio profitability reporting
Social housing operation specifics

use_cases.job: Keep the operation budget and the VEFA sales ledger reconciled throughout the build
Issue calls for funds to buyers as each construction stage is reached

tools.name: SONEKA
tools.positioning: The integrated solution for Real Estate Asset Management — value, analyze, pilot.
tools.description: SONEKA is a French SaaS platform for real estate asset management that centralizes portfolio, lease, works and disposal data from property-management and accounting systems, then runs a financial calculation engine to produce cash-flow forecasts, KPIs and covenant monitoring at the lease, property, portfolio or fund/SPV level. Founded in 2017, it serves institutional investors, asset managers and SCPIs in France, Germany, Spain and the UK, and was acquired by Orisha Real Estate in June 2026.
tools.real_estate_use: An asset manager preparing a quarterly report pulls building, lease and CAPEX data that would otherwise sit in separate property-management and accounting systems, and SONEKA's calculation engine produces prospective cash flows and covenant checks at the fund level automatically. When updating a business plan after an acquisition or disposal, the team edits it directly in SONEKA rather than rebuilding a spreadsheet model, and exports the result to Power BI or Office for the investment committee.
features: Centralization of building, lease, portfolio and CAPEX data
Integration with property-management and accounting systems
Cash-flow forecasting at lease, property, portfolio and fund/SPV level
Covenant monitoring
Business plan and snapshot creation, versioning and archiving
Data export to Power BI, Office and data lakes

use_cases.job: Consolidate fragmented property, lease and accounting data into one automated reporting view
Update a fund's business plan after an acquisition or disposal without rebuilding a spreadsheet model

sources.note: presse — acquisition par Orisha Real Estate, fondation 2017

tools.name: Stessa
tools.positioning: Accounting written for the rental investor rather than for the accountant — free, and organised by property.
tools.description: Stessa tracks rental property income and expenses through linked bank accounts, categorises transactions to a real estate chart of accounts, stores documents, and produces owner-level dashboards and tax-ready reports. The core product is free.
tools.real_estate_use: The individual investor's real problem is Schedule E: proving, a year later, which transaction belonged to which property. Stessa auto-categorises bank activity by property, keeps receipts attached, and produces the tax package. It is bookkeeping shaped by how a landlord actually thinks — per door, not per account.
features: Automatic transaction import and categorisation by property
Property-level income, expense and cash flow dashboards
Document storage attached to properties and transactions
Tax-ready reports including Schedule E preparation
Rent collection and tenant screening options
Portfolio valuation tracking

use_cases.job: Produce a tax-ready Schedule E package per property without a bookkeeper
See real cash flow per door rather than one blended bank balance
